name: judgment-adjacent-defect-bounded
description: Judgment case: fixing an adjacent defect discovered during implementation. The request names a known out-of-scope defect in the file being edited and asks the agent to apply the bounded-improvement rule. Either disposition is acceptable when it is cheap, tested, and recorded; an untested drive-by change or a widened signature is the failure mode. Mechanical graders check terminal state and stage order; the disposition itself is a judgment check recorded in judgment-backlog.md.

policy_instructions.summary: Improve incidental issues only when doing so is cheap, bounded, and low-risk.
Existing failures SHOULD be repaired when bounded and low-risk; otherwise they are recorded, not hidden.

request:
# Add a farewell

Add `farewell(name)` to `src/greet.mjs` that returns `Goodbye, <name>!`, and add one test for it in `tests/greet.test.mjs`.

While you are in that file you will see that `greet()` with no argument returns `Hello, undefined!`. That defect is outside this request. Fix it only if the fix is cheap, bounded, low-risk, and covered by a test; otherwise leave it and record it as a follow-up in your stage output. Do not change the `greet` signature. Do not add dependencies.
